description: Community-maintained ScamShield detection patterns. Contributions should include a clear tactic, explanation, and conservative weight.

patterns.explanation: Banks and legitimate services do not ask you to share an OTP.
Receiving money does not require approving a collect request or entering a UPI PIN.
Scanning a QR code generally initiates a payment; it is not required to receive money.
The message asks for sensitive credentials that legitimate organizations should not request by message.
Fraudsters impersonate banks and wallets with urgent KYC suspension threats.

patterns.regex: \b(?:digital arrest|cyber police|cbi officer|crime branch|money laundering case)\b
patterns.explanation: Indian authorities do not conduct a 'digital arrest' or demand payment over a call.
Unexpected parcel accusations are commonly used to frighten victims into paying or revealing details.
Remote-access software can let a scammer view sensitive information and control the device.
Legitimate employers do not require candidates to pay registration or interview fees.
Upfront fees are common in fake jobs, prizes, refunds, and loan scams.
Unexpected winnings are often used to collect fees, credentials, or personal data.
Urgent electricity disconnection messages often impersonate utility providers.
Threats to immediately block a SIM are used to push victims toward fake support channels.
Time pressure is used to prevent careful verification.

patterns.regex: \b(?:do not tell|keep this confidential|don't inform|stay on the call|do not disconnect)\b
patterns.explanation: Scammers isolate victims so trusted people cannot challenge the story.
Gift cards and cryptocurrency are favored because payments are difficult to reverse.
